answer: We define a mechanism where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds require validators to commit collateral, effectively turning any potential Sybil inlet into a high-friction financial liability. Subgame-perfect punishment matrices force slashing penalties to exceed the cumulative rewards of identity multiplication, leaving an ember of lost capital for any agent attempting to fracture their stake. In this meadow of Byzantine agents, negative expected utility for cloning ensures Nash equilibrium convergence, as rational actors reject non-profitable attacks.
